lines: On a public blockchain, every balance, every trade, and every counterparty is visible to everyone. Forever.
Antumbra is a shielded pool with batch swaps, built on NEAR.
Shield your tokens, and they cross from the light into the shade.
The chain sees an amount and a commitment. Never who owns it.
Inside the shade, transfers are private.
The chain sees two nullifiers and two commitments, and nothing else.
Swaps are batched by epoch, and every amount is sealed: encrypted inside the proof, so not even the chain learns it.
When the epoch ends, the sealer opens the batch and publishes only the totals.
Everyone trades at one clearing price, and claims their share privately.
Every action is a single {Groth16|Groth sixteen} proof.
It is built in your browser in seconds, and verified on chain by NEAR's native {BLS12-381|B L S twelve, three eighty-one} host functions.
Inside a batch, buyers and sellers net against each other.
Only the imbalance needs outside liquidity, and that leg is priced live on NEAR Intents.
And it runs today. A wallet that proves in the browser, live on NEAR testnet, with wrapped NEAR and {USDC|U S D C}.
Shield, swap, claim, and withdraw, and see exactly what the chain saw.
Three circuits, a Rust contract, a browser wallet, a command line wallet, and a sealer built for a {TEE|trusted execution environment}.
Open source, and tested end to end.
Antumbra. Private transfers, sealed swaps, one price per epoch.
